review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

6:1.sourceText: Διὸ ἀφέντες τὸν τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα φερώμεθα, μὴ πάλιν θεμέλιον καταβαλλόμενοι μετανοίας ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, καὶ πίστεως ἐπὶ Θεόν,
6:1.targetText: For this reason, having left the word of the beginning of the Christ, we may advance to perfection, not laying again a foundation of conversion from dead works, and of faith on God,

groups.note: The actual passive/middle movement form φερώμεθα means let us be carried/press forward; LSV we may advance retains that movement head without inventing a different Greek advancing verb.
The actual μετάνοια repentance/change-of-mind noun is rendered conversion, retaining that head rather than a different turning noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:2.sourceText: βαπτισμῶν διδαχὴν, ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν, ἀναστάσεώς νεκρῶν, καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου.
6:2.targetText: of the teaching of immersions, also of laying on of hands, also of [the] resurrection of the dead, and of continuous judgment,

groups.note: The actual βαπτισμός plural names washings/immersions; its original noun stays distinct from the separate βάπτισμα noun, without deciding here whether the ritual reference is ceremonial or Christian.

Pinned N1904 διδαχήν is accusative teaching in the foundation/list construction; LSV recasts it as genitive of the teaching, following the genitive reading. The same teaching head is retained with the case/attachment difference explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats an additive also before resurrection; N1904 has the earlier τε at laying-on and its closing καί before judgment, without an additional connector at resurrection.
English supplies the bracketed article before resurrection; the actual resurrection noun is anarthrous.

6:3.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσομεν, ἐάνπερ ἐπιτρέπῃ ὁ Θεός.
6:3.targetText: and this we will do, if God may permit,

6:4.sourceText: Ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς ἐπουρανίου καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας Πνεύματος Ἁγίου
6:4.targetText: for [it is] impossible for those once enlightened, having also tasted of the heavenly gift, and having become partakers of the Holy Spirit,

groups.note: The actual accusative nominalizer τοὺς introduces the once-enlightened people who are the object of renewing across6:4–6. LSV fronts them as for those and resumes the same actual patients as bracketed them at6:6. No independent Greek for preposition or later object pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The second attributive article qualifies gift as heavenly; LSV uses the heavenly gift with one article rather than a second relative/article word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

6:5.sourceText: καὶ καλὸν γευσαμένους Θεοῦ ῥῆμα δυνάμεις τε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος,
6:5.targetText: and tasted the good saying of God, also the powers of the coming age,

6:6.sourceText: καὶ παραπεσόντας, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἀνασταυροῦντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας.
6:6.targetText: and having fallen away, to renew [them] again to conversion, having crucified to themselves the Son of God again, and exposed to public shame.

groups.note: The actual present crucifying-anew participle ἀνασταυροῦντας is rendered having crucified ... again by LSV. Its actual compound head supplies again, while the separate πάλιν earlier belongs to renewing again. The source present participle is not a written perfect/aorist merely because English uses having.

The actual present public-shaming participle παραδειγματίζοντας is rendered exposed to public shame under the English having construction. This keeps the one real shame/exposure head without separate Greek public or shame-noun tokens.

The actual accusative people nominalizer at6:4 introduces the patients of this renewing infinitive. English resumes the same once-enlightened/fallen people as bracketed them here, preserving that original identity across the long sentence. The word remains rendered at6:4 too, so this is shared identity rather than an exclusively moved word.

6:7.sourceText: γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ἐρχόμενον πολλάκις ὑετόν καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις δι’ οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ·
6:7.targetText: For the earth, having drunk in the rain coming on it many times, and is bringing forth herbs fit for those because of whom it is also dressed, partakes of blessing from God,

groups.note: The actual attributive article introduces the drinking modifier of this same earth noun; LSV places its definite article directly with earth and renders the modifier as having drunk. The article remains within the same earth noun phrase.
The actual producing/bearing participle τίκτουσα is recast as is bringing forth; the English auxiliary belongs to this written verbal predicate.
The actual passive cultivation verb γεωργεῖται is rendered is dressed in the agricultural sense; it is not a Greek clothing verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:8.sourceText: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀδόκιμος καὶ κατάρας ἐγγύς, ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν.
6:8.targetText: but that which is bearing thorns and briers [is] disapproved of, and near to cursing, whose end [is] for burning;

groups.note: The actual feminine bearing participle continues the earth subject and is expanded by LSV as that which is bearing. The English nominal/relative support expresses that real predicate without an additional source earth noun or relative pronoun.
The actual unapproved/unfit adjective ἀδόκιμος is rendered disapproved of; it is not a written passive disapproving verb, so its English copula remains separately supplied.

6:9.sourceText: Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, εἰ καὶ οὕτως λαλοῦμεν.
6:9.targetText: but we are persuaded, concerning you, beloved, the things that are better, and accompanying salvation, though even thus we speak,

groups.note: The actual middle having/being-connected participle ἐχόμενα denotes things belonging closely to salvation; LSV accompanying preserves that relation, not a substituted Greek walking/following verb.
The concessive εἰ καί construction means though/although; LSV though even expresses the full concession, not an isolated universal εἰ=though rule.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the nominal things-that-are-better modifier; the actual persuaded verb supports the earlier we are persuaded and is not moved into this adjective phrase.

6:10.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τοῦ ἔργου ὑμῶν καὶ τῆς ἀγάπης ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονοῦντες.
6:10.targetText: for God is not unrighteous to forget your work, and the labor of love that you showed to His Name, having ministered to the holy ones and ministering;

groups.note: The actual love noun is coordinated with work as the genitive object of forget; LSV inserts labor and recasts love as labor of love. The love head remains with its real source while the added labor is separately explained.

6:11.sourceText: ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους,
6:11.targetText: and we desire each one of you to show the same diligence, to the full assurance of the hope to the end,

groups.note: The actual substantive quantifier ἕκαστον names each one of the people; one makes that pronominal role explicit, not a separate Greek numeral.

6:12.sourceText: ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε, μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονομούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας.
6:12.targetText: that you may not become slothful, but followers of those who through faith and patient endurance are inheriting the promises.

groups.note: The actual imitators noun μιμηταί is rendered followers in the exemplar-following sense, not a substituted Greek following verb or follower noun.

6:13.sourceText: Τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ Θεός, ἐπεὶ κατ’ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθ’ ἑαυτοῦ,
6:13.targetText: For God, having made promise to Abraham, seeing He was not able to swear by [any] greater, swore by Himself,

groups.note: Greek οὐδενὸς εἶχεν says He had no one greater by whom to swear; LSV recasts that absence of a greater oath-authority as He was not able to swear by any greater. The negative-indefinite and having predicate jointly support this modal wording, not a bare ἔχω=δύναμαι lexical substitution.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:14.sourceText: λέγων Εἰ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε·
6:14.targetText: saying, “Blessing I will indeed bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you”;

groups.note: The pinned εἰ μήν is the affirmative assurance formula in an oath, documented as surely/assuredly at Hebrews6:14 (Thayer1487), not the negative μή particle or the negative-rest oath. LSV indeed retains the whole actual formula without changing its raw words.

6:15.sourceText: καὶ οὕτως μακροθυμήσας ἐπέτυχεν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας.
6:15.targetText: and so, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise;

6:16.sourceText: ἄνθρωποι γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ μείζονος ὀμνύουσιν, καὶ πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος·
6:16.targetText: for men swear by the greater, and the oath [is] for confirmation of the end of all their controversy,

groups.note: The actual dative to them identifies the disputing people; English recasts that relation as their controversy without a separately written possessive form.

The actual πέρας is the predicate end/limit of all dispute. LSV makes that same end noun dependent on confirmation as confirmation of the end; its added of is separately explained rather than claiming the original end noun is genitive.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English embeds the actual predicate end under confirmation with of the end; Greek has end as the oath’s predicate, not a genitive complement of confirmation.

6:17.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ περισσότερον βουλόμενος ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιδεῖξαι τοῖς κληρονόμοις τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὸ ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς αὐτοῦ ἐμεσίτευσεν ὅρκῳ,
6:17.targetText: in which God, more abundantly willing to show to the heirs of the promise the immutability of His counsel, interposed by an oath,

groups.note: The actual unchangeable adjective ἀμετάθετον is substantival for the unchangeable quality; LSV renders the abstraction as immutability, not a separately written Greek quality noun.
The actual mediating/intervening verb ἐμεσίτευσεν is rendered interposed in the oath assurance, not a different Greek inserting verb.

6:18.sourceText: ἵνα διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων, ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύσασθαι Θεόν, ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆσαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος·
6:18.targetText: that through two immutable things, in which [it is] impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong comfort, having fled for refuge, to lay hold on the hope being set before [us],

groups.note: The actual accusative God is the subject of the lying infinitive; English for God states that same infinitival-subject relation without an independently written Greek for preposition.

The actual οἱ καταφυγόντες whole substantival participle designates we, the refuge-fleeing people, appositional to the first-person plural having predicate. These same actual people are the recipients before whom hope is set, resumed as bracketed us in English. The whole written person construction supports both having fled for refuge and us; the article alone is not treated as an inferred object pronoun, and no independent Greek us word is invented.

6:19.sourceText: ἣν ὡς ἄγκυραν ἔχομεν τῆς ψυχῆς ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ βεβαίαν καὶ εἰσερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος,
6:19.targetText: which we have, as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and entering into that within the veil,

groups.note: The actual inner-region adjective ἐσώτερον is substantival under the article, that within the veil. LSV within retains its inner-side spatial relation rather than a different Greek within preposition.

6:20.sourceText: ὅπου πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς, κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἀρχιερεὺς γενόμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
6:20.targetText: to where a forerunner entered for us—Jesus, having become Chief Priest throughout the age after the order of Melchizedek.

groups.note: The actual where adverb ὅπου identifies the place entered; English to where states its directional relation to entered without a separately written Greek to preposition.
Greek κατά expresses conformity to the order; English after the order uses after in that pattern/conformity sense, not as a chronological after marker.
